get.description: Retrieve the logs of your container. Requires a v2 endpoint storage. Logs are returned from the active container while the deployment is running, and from your S3 bucket once the deployment has been terminated. Lifecycle events and restart history are available through the same endpoint.

parameters.description: Optional. Which run of your container to read logs from. Every time the container crashes and is restarted this counter goes up by one (the first run is 0). Leave it empty to read the most recent run; only set it to look back at the logs of an earlier crash.
parameters.name: restart

parameters.description: Optional. The logs of a single run are split into numbered pieces ("chunks") once they grow large; this selects one piece by its number. Leave it empty to get the newest logs: the live tail while the deployment is running, or the last saved piece once it has stopped. Only set it to page back through older logs of the selected run.
parameters.name: chunk

parameters.description: Optional. How the log lines are returned. `text` (the default) gives plain, human-readable lines. `ndjson` gives one JSON object per line, carrying each line's stream and timestamp, useful for log tooling.
parameters.name: format

get.description: Stream the live logs of your container as Server-Sent Events. Requires a v2 endpoint storage and a running (non-terminated) deployment. Each event payload contains a single JSON-encoded log line.

200.description: The client's enabled global caching configurations.

get.description: Lists all of your enabled global caching configurations, one per cached build. A build absent from this list has global caching disabled.

200.description: Your global caching quota and usage.

get.description: Returns how much global caching your plan allows and how much of it your cached builds take up. Use it to work out whether a new build fits before enabling caching on it, and which builds to uncache if it does not. A limit of null means your plan sets no limit.

404.description: The build is not addressable by the calling client.

503.description: Caching could not be reached. Retrying later may succeed.

200.description: Caching disabled. Returns the build and the versions that were affected.

delete.summary: [v2] Disable Global Caching for a Build
delete.description: Disables global caching for this build and returns the versions that were affected, so you can confirm the blast radius of the eviction. The status change is immediate; teardown of the underlying per-version caches is asynchronous.

503.description: The registry of the build could not be reached. Retrying later may succeed.

409.description: A caching quota limit has been reached.

404.description: The build is not addressable by the calling client.

422.description: The build is in a state you have to resolve before it can be cached: its registry did not serve it, or it resolves to something that cannot be cached.

200.description: Caching enabled, newly or already. Returns the configuration and affected versions.

put.summary: [v2] Enable Global Caching for a Build
put.description: Enables global caching for this build. Idempotent: re-enabling returns the current configuration. The status change is immediate; materialization of the underlying per-version caches is asynchronous. The body is empty and exists only to host future optional configuration fields.

404.description: Global caching is disabled for this build, or the build is not addressable.

200.description: Caching is enabled. Returns the configuration and affected versions.

get.summary: [v2] Get the Global Caching status of a Build
get.description: Returns the global caching configuration when caching is enabled for this build. A 404 means caching is disabled, not that the build is missing: build existence is established via GET /builds.

info.title: Edgegap V2
info.description: We are pleased to introduce the V2 version of our API.

API Token.name: Authorization
API Token.description: 🔒 **Authentication Required** To use the Edgegap API, you need an API token. Follow these steps: 1. Go to **Dashboard › Account Settings › Tokens**. 2. Generate or view your API token. 3. Include the token in your API requests using the `Authorization` header: **Header format:** ``` Authorization: token your-secret-token-here ``` Make sure to include the word `token` before your actual token.
